candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — peripheral IV catheter monitoring
candidate.educational_objective: Apply current CDC guidance by monitoring adult peripheral IV sites and acting on clinical indications without falsely treating clinically indicated-only replacement as a universal CDC mandate.

options.A: Routine replacement should occur more frequently than every 72 hours to reduce infection risk.
options.B: Assess the site regularly and remove or replace the catheter for clinical indications such as phlebitis, infection, or malfunction, while following the organization's replacement policy.
options.C: Every adult peripheral IV may remain in place indefinitely unless infusion completely stops.
options.D: CDC mandates replacement only when clinically indicated for every adult peripheral IV.

candidate.rationale: CDC states that adult peripheral catheters do not need routine replacement more frequently than every 72–96 hours. CDC makes no recommendation for clinically indicated-only replacement in adults because that remains an unresolved issue. However, catheter sites should be assessed regularly and catheters removed for phlebitis, infection, malfunction, or other clinical indication. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Adult peripheral catheters need not be replaced more often than every 72–96 hours; clinically indicated-only replacement in adults is an unresolved issue; sites require regular assessment and catheter removal for clinical problems.
